name: Pastry for Cornish Pasties
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors

ingredients.item: ½ lb (225 g) mixture of lard, butter, and/or suet (equal ratios)

steps: Combine the dry ingredients, then gradually mix in enough water to make a stiff dough.
Roll dough to about a ¼ inch thick.
Cut out rounds with a tea plate—or other round object about 6in across.
Lay rounds on a pastry-board with half the round propped on a rolling-pin. Add the filling, and fold dough over filling.
Dampen the edges with water, and press to seal. Crimp the edges, then make slit in middle of each pasty.
Place on baking sheet, bake in hot oven (450°F) until golden-brown.

culture.text: A pasty is a British baked turnover, a variety of which is particularly associated with Cornwall and Devon but has spread all over the United Kingdom and elsewhere through the Cornish diaspora. It consists of a filling, typically meat and vegetables, baked in a folded and crimped shortcrust pastry circle.
